en: That divine name which causes the cycle of worldly existence to become like a cow’s footprint for those who remember it—that is true devotion; I take refuge in that state of Rāma.
Oṃ! May He protect us both; may He nourish us both; may we work together with vigor; may our study be brilliant; may we not harbor mutual hatred. Oṃ! Peace! Peace! Peace!

Hari, Oṃ! At the end of the Dvāpara age, Nārada went to Brahmā and asked, "O Blessed One, how may I cross over the Kali age while wandering the earth? Brahmā said to him, "I have been well questioned. Listen to that secret of all the Vedas which must be guarded, by means of which you shall cross the worldly ocean of Kali. Merely by the utterance of the name of the Blessed Ādipuruṣa Nārāyaṇa, one becomes cleansed of the Kali age. || 1 ||
Nārada asked again, "What is its name? He replied, "It is Hiraṇyagarbha.
*Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare;
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare.*
Thus, this set of sixteen names destroys the impurities of the Kali age;
no means superior to this is seen in all the Vedas.

When the covering of the individual soul (jīva), which is enveloped by sixteen kalās, is destroyed, then the supreme Brahman shines forth, like the orb of the sun's rays when the clouds have vanished. || 2 ||

Nārada asked again: "O Blessed One, what is the ritual injunction for this? He said to him: "There is no ritual injunction for this. Whether always pure or impure, a Brāhmaṇa who recites it attains the same world, proximity, similarity of form, and union [with Brahman]. When he recites sixteen and a half million of these, he crosses over the murder of a Brāhmaṇa; he crosses over the murder of a hero; he becomes purified from the theft of gold; he becomes purified from sexual intercourse with a low-caste woman (vṛṣalī); he becomes purified from offenses against the ancestors, the gods, and human beings."
One attains immediate purity from the sin of abandoning all dharmas; one is immediately liberated, one is immediately liberated—this is the Upaniṣad.

Oṃ. May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together; may we work together with great vigor; may our study be luminous; may we never harbor enmity toward one another. Oṃ. Peace! Peace! Peace!
